h1:
Suphan Buri Cafes
9 In-Town + Rice-Field Spots
intro: Suphan Buri is an easy place to get around — short distances, just a few minutes' drive from one spot to the next — which makes it perfect for slotting a cafe between temples, the Sam Chuk market, or the Banharn-Jamsai Tower. The town has two kinds of cafes to match the rhythm of your day: in-town shops that are easy to reach and easy to park at, and rice-field or Tha Chin River cafes that are barely outside town but open up to wide, breezy views. We picked 9 that are actually open right now, with the neighborhood, signature drinks, and rough prices for each.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Suphan Buri cafes is that you don't have to drive far. The town is compact, so most in-town shops are only a few minutes apart, and the rice-field and riverside cafes usually sit within 15–20 minutes of the center. So we've split them into two groups — the first for days when you're walking around town and want a seat close by, the second for days when you're after open-air rice-field views. Just pick whichever suits your mood that day.

This group is the reason a lot of people drive out to Suphan Buri in the first place — wide green rice fields, a cool breeze in the morning or late afternoon. Some sit right on the Tha Chin River, others look out toward distant hills. They're made for settling in, taking photos, and grabbing a light bite.

items.name: Ban Rim Na Cafe
items.blurb: It does exactly what the name says — a Thai-style house looking straight out over the rice fields, with a relaxed, unfussy, homespun feel. They serve drinks alongside Thai sweets, and it's a good place to sit back and shoot the field views without fighting anyone for an angle. Opens mid-morning and runs to early evening.

items.name: Chomchan Cafe & Somtum Bar
items.blurb: A wide lawn backed by hills that makes you feel like you've wandered off to some far-flung province, plus a paddock area with sheep to walk around. The draw here is that it's a cafe and a somtum (papaya salad) bar in one — come with a group and make a real meal of it, not just a coffee.
items.meta: Hill + field view · open 08:00–20:00 · food + coffee 60–150 THB

items.name: Phop The Riverside Cafe
items.blurb: A Thai-style house on the river, ringed by big shade trees, calm and cool — better suited to people who want water over rice fields. The menu runs from drinks and desserts to dishes built around local ingredients. Come in the late afternoon for the nicer light.

items.name: Double P Home Cafe'
items.blurb: A homey cafe around Bang Pla Ma, tucked under big shade trees with a riverside zone too, and dogs are welcome. The vibe is warm, like a friend's place. One thing to know: it only opens Saturday and Sunday, so it'll be closed on a weekday — check before you set out.
items.meta: Bang Pla Ma area · weekends only 09:00–18:00 · coffee 55–85 THB

items.name: Mueang Noe Coffee
items.blurb: Set in the middle of a mango orchard — shady and cool, with a man-made sandy beach for a bit of a seaside feel. The most-ordered items are the Mueang Noe coffee, the crab bread, and the mango chicken stir-fry. Parking is limited, so mornings or evenings are the easier bet.
items.meta: Mango orchard · open 09:30–20:00 (closed Wed) · coffee + food 55–140 THB

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: A lot of the rice-field cafes don't have much shade, and the sun gets strong from around 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. If you want to sit outside comfortably and catch softer light for photos, go before 10 a.m. or from about 3 p.m. onward. And several out-of-town spots close on Wednesdays — check the opening day before you drive out.

blocks.text: In-town cafes — easy to reach, easy to park

blocks.html: If you're spending the day around town — the Banharn-Jamsai Tower, Wat Pa Lelai, the old-town markets — this group sits close by and is easy to drop into. Most are serious coffee shops that roast their own or run a slow bar, so they're for people who'd rather have a great cup than a view.

items.name: No.5 Cafe Suphanburi
items.blurb: A white-toned cafe built around natural light, open and airy, popular with the photo crowd and people getting work done. There's coffee, non-coffee drinks, bakery items, and one-plate meals, so you can settle in for a while.
items.meta: In town · Mon–Fri 07:30–16:00 / Sat–Sun 08:00–17:00 (closed Wed) · coffee 50–75 THB

items.name: Zimply Coffee Roaster
items.blurb: A genuine coffee shop that roasts its beans in-house, with a dark, homey-industrial look. The regulars order the Dirty Latte and the macchiato, and there's craft cocoa too. A good fit if you like a strong cup to start the morning.

items.name: Rom Coffee & Bakeroom
items.blurb: Clean and minimal, with both a Speed Bar and a Slow Bar so you can take your pick. The standout is the homemade bakery, baked fresh every day, and the photo corners are nice. A good stop for pastries alongside a solid coffee.
items.meta: In town · open 09:00–18:00 (closed Tue) · coffee 55–80 THB

items.name: U DOM Coffee Slow Bar
items.blurb: A small, simple shop near the Banharn-Jamsai Tower, focused on slow bar and espresso, with a relaxed homespun feel. It's the kind of place for a single proper cup before you carry on sightseeing — not somewhere you settle in for hours, but the coffee is good.
items.meta: Near Banharn-Jamsai Tower · open 07:30–17:30 · coffee 45–70 THB

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: In-town coffee shops like Zimply and U DOM close in the afternoon, so if you want a serious house-roasted cup, plan to stop in from the morning to early afternoon. The sit-a-while cafes like No.5 and Rom stay open later into the evening — better for winding down the day.

blocks.text: How to match a cafe to your day

items: Around town all day — go for No.5, Rom, or U DOM, all easy to reach and easy to slot in between the Banharn-Jamsai Tower and Wat Pa Lelai.
After rice-field views + photos — Ban Rim Na or Chomchan are the most wide-open. Come in the morning or late afternoon for nicer light and less heat.
Coming as a group for a real meal — Chomchan (with somtum) or Mueang Noe Coffee (with mains) can fill you up properly, not just with coffee.
Serious about coffee — Zimply roasts its own, and Rom has both a speed and slow bar; both put the cup ahead of the view.
Bringing the dog — Double P Home Cafe' takes pets, but remember it only opens Saturday and Sunday.

blocks.text: Timing and what to know before you go

blocks.html: Suphan Buri's rice fields change with the season. Early in the rainy season (June–July) the fields are at their greenest, so the rice-field cafes look better than in the dry months. In the cool season (November–January) the weather is just right, and you can sit outside comfortably all day.

items: Several shops close Wednesday or Tuesday — especially the out-of-town ones. Always check the opening day on Google Maps before you drive out.
Out-of-town parking can be limited — at spots like Mueang Noe Coffee, mornings or evenings make it easier to find a space.
Carry some cash — a few small cafes take only cash or PromptPay, so don't count on cards alone.
Prices here are rough estimates — drinks generally run about 45–90 THB and one-plate meals around 80–150 THB, and they can shift with the menu and time of day.

faq.q: Which Suphan Buri cafes have the best rice-field views?
faq.a: Ban Rim Na Cafe is a Thai-style house looking straight out over the rice fields, with a relaxed, homespun feel. Chomchan Cafe has a wide lawn backed by hills and a sheep paddock. Both are good for photos and settling in for a while — go in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the harsh sun.

faq.q: Which in-town Suphan Buri cafes are easy to stop by while sightseeing?
faq.a: No.5 Cafe is white-toned and open, good for working; Rom Coffee & Bakeroom bakes fresh every day; and U DOM Coffee Slow Bar sits near the Banharn-Jamsai Tower, ideal for a single cup before you move on. All are in town and easy to park at.

faq.q: Which Suphan Buri cafes serve a proper meal, not just coffee?
faq.a: Chomchan Cafe has somtum and other dishes to order, while Mueang Noe Coffee has mains like the mango chicken stir-fry and crab bread. Both are good for coming as a group and making a real meal of it, not just drinks and sweets.

faq.q: What days do Suphan Buri cafes usually close?
faq.a: Several out-of-town shops close on Wednesday, such as Mueang Noe Coffee, while some close on Tuesday, like Rom and Phop The Riverside. Double P Home Cafe' only opens Saturday and Sunday. Always check the opening day on Google Maps before you set out.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost at Suphan Buri cafes?
faq.a: Drinks generally run about 45–90 THB depending on the shop and the menu, while one-plate meals at cafes with a kitchen run around 80–150 THB — easygoing prices overall. These are rough estimates and can shift with the menu and time of day.
